title: Monterey Cypress: Old Monterey Cypresses You Can Visit
meta_description: Wild on two Californian headlands and nowhere else. The Lone Cypress above Carmel Bay, seeded around 1750, is one of the few trees with a trademark.
intro: In the wild this tree grows on two headlands near Monterey in California and nowhere else on earth, together covering less than a square kilometre. The Lone Cypress grows out of a granite headland above Carmel Bay by itself, propped by a retaining wall and steel cables since the 1940s; it was probably seeded around 1750, close to the ceiling for its species, and the Pebble Beach Company has held a trademark on its drawing since 1919. The Old Veteran at Point Lobos has been painted since 1879. Give the species a mild wet winter anywhere and it grows fast and enormous, which is how it reached Italian and Portuguese gardens within a few decades of being described. Trieste's stands at Miramare, put in after 1856, and Lucca's on the San Regolo bastion of the city's Renaissance walls.
